bugs.error_message: Dashboard 'Repositories' list empty / 'fetch-repositories' returns no repos when Start Scan clicked
bugs.root_cause: GITHUB_TOKEN in .env is expired/invalid — GitHub API returns 401 on https://api.github.com/users/<username>/repos. Confirmed via server log '[repos] GitHub 401 — Token expired or invalid' and direct curl to api.github.com/user returning 401.
bugs.fix: User must regenerate a GitHub PAT at github.com/settings/tokens (classic, scopes: repo + read:user) and update GITHUB_TOKEN in .env, then restart `npm start`.

bugs.error_message: SonarQube scan fails: 'ERROR: Not authorized. Please check the user token in the property sonar.token or sonar.login'
bugs.root_cause: SONAR_TOKEN in .env was invalid/expired — confirmed via curl -u <token>: http://localhost:9000/api/authentication/validate returning {"valid":false}.
bugs.fix: Generated a fresh token via SonarQube API using admin credentials: curl -u admin:<password> -X POST http://localhost:9000/api/user_tokens/generate -d name=<name>. Updated SONAR_TOKEN in .env, then force-killed the stale node.exe holding port 3002 (TaskStop alone did not release it — same as bug-026) and restarted npm start.

bugs.error_message: AI Review returns 'API key is invalid' even though .env's ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is a valid (just credit-exhausted) key
bugs.root_cause: A stale ANTHROPIC_API_KEY was already set at the Windows User+Machine environment-variable level (verified via [Environment]::GetEnvironmentVariable). dotenv.config() does NOT override existing process.env values by default, so the OS-level (invalid) key silently won over the correct .env value — server startup log 'AI Key: Set' was misleading since it didn't reveal which source won.
bugs.fix: Changed require('dotenv').config() to require('dotenv').config({ override: true }) in server.js so .env always takes precedence over stale OS-level env vars of the same name. Confirmed the real Anthropic key in .env is valid but out of credit balance (direct curl to api.anthropic.com/v1/messages returns 'Your credit balance is too low') — that is a separate, account-level issue the user needs to resolve at console.anthropic.com/settings/billing, not a code bug.

bugs.error_message: Quality rating badges rendered as '1.0' / '2.0' instead of A–E letters, and the rating-X CSS class never matched
bugs.root_cause: SonarQube's /api/measures/component returns reliability_rating, security_rating and sqale_rating as numeric strings ('1.0'..'5.0'), not letters. The frontend interpolated the raw value straight into both the badge text and the class name: class="rating rating-${m.reliability_rating||'A'}" produced the non-existent class 'rating-1.0'.
bugs.fix: Added a ratingLetter(v) helper in public/index.html that maps 1..5 to A..E (and passes through values that are already letters), used everywhere a rating is displayed — the scan-complete result panel and the new Scan History table.

bugs.error_message: Overview cards 'AZURE ORG' and project name always showed '—'
bugs.root_cause: Leftover from the Azure DevOps era: the frontend read cfg.org and cfg.project from /api/config, but the GitHub-based server only returns githubUsername, sonarUrl and repoBasePath. Those keys never existed, so the cards were permanently empty. Several other Azure labels were also stale ('Fetching from Azure DevOps...', 'Azure API unreachable', fa-microsoft pipeline icon).
bugs.fix: Rewrote config handling into loadServerConfig()/applyServerConfig(); the tile now shows the GitHub account from cfg.githubUsername. Extended /api/config in server.js with integration status booleans (githubConfigured, sonarConfigured, aiConfigured, smtpConfigured), aiModel, notifyEmail and smtpHost — booleans only, never secret values. Replaced all remaining Azure DevOps wording and the fa-microsoft icon with GitHub equivalents.

bugs.error_message: Potential TypeError on scan completion: document.getElementById('recent-scans').innerHTML after the sidebar rebuild removed that element
bugs.root_cause: The scan-complete socket handler wrote into a 'recent-scans' sidebar block. The dashboard rebuild replaced the sidebar with grouped navigation and dropped that element, which would have thrown on the next completed scan.
bugs.fix: Replaced the sidebar write with recordScanRun(), which persists the run to localStorage ('sonarai.scanHistory') and feeds both the Scan History page and the Overview 'Latest Scan Runs' card. Also added an id-reference audit (all getElementById/$ calls cross-checked against ids present in the file) to catch this class of breakage after markup edits.

bugs.error_message: A viewer or reviewer could never change their own password
bugs.root_cause: changeOwnPassword() initially called PATCH /api/users/:id, which is guarded by requirePerm('users.edit'). Only admins hold that permission, so every non-admin got a 403 when rotating their own credentials.
bugs.fix: Added POST /api/auth/password — session-only (no permission required), but requires the current password and enforces the 8-character minimum. The frontend self-service form now posts there; the admin reset path via PATCH /api/users/:id is unchanged.

bugs.error_message: User Management showed 'Total Users 0 / Admins 0 / Active 0' to viewers and reviewers
bugs.root_cause: The four stat tiles stayed visible for roles without users.view. Since loadUsers() returns early for those roles, the tiles kept their initial 0 values — reading as 'this agent has no users' rather than 'you cannot see this'.
bugs.fix: Gave the tile row id 'um-tiles' and hid it in gateUiByPermission() whenever users.view is absent, leaving only the explanatory permission-denied note.

bugs.error_message: GitHub PAT printed in plaintext on every git command
bugs.root_cause: gitExec logged its raw argv, which includes `-c http.extraheader=AUTHORIZATION: basic <base64>`, and that base64 decodes to "<user>:<GITHUB_TOKEN>". Every fetch/checkout/pull wrote a working credential to the console, server.log and the background task output. safeError also lacked a github_pat_ pattern, so the fine-grained token was only partly masked even where safeError was applied.
bugs.fix: Added redactGitArgs() to mask the extraheader argument before logging, routed gitExec stdout/stderr through safeError, and extended safeError with explicit github_pat_, gho_/ghs_ and sqp_/squ_ patterns. Verified git history and tracked files never contained the token — the leak was console/log only.

bugs.error_message: git: 'sonar-scanner.cmd' is not a git command. See 'git --help'.
bugs.root_cause: The scanner presence check called gitExec([scannerCmd, '-v']), which runs `git sonar-scanner.cmd -v`. Git has no such subcommand so it always threw; the scanner was only ever found via the fallback branch, after logging a misleading git error every scan.
bugs.fix: Replaced with a direct runCommand(`${scannerCmd} -v`) call and removed the now-redundant fallback branch.

bugs.error_message: Scan died with "Fail to get bootstrap index from server", then follow-up API calls failed with an empty `reason:`
bugs.root_cause: SonarQube was not running on :9000 and nothing checked first. The scanner burned a minute before failing, then /api/projects/create and /api/issues/search failed with node-fetch errors whose reason string was blank, hiding the real cause. Root cause was environmental, not code — but the pipeline gave no usable signal.
bugs.fix: Added a /api/system/status preflight before every scan that fails immediately with actionable instructions, and distinguishes STARTING (wait) from unreachable (start StartSonar.bat). Note: SonarQube takes ~2 minutes to go from launch to status UP.

bugs.root_cause: SMTP_PASS is empty in .env but sendEmail only guarded on SMTP_HOST, so nodemailer attempted PLAIN auth with a blank password and failed opaquely on every notification.
bugs.fix: sendEmail now returns early when SMTP_USER or SMTP_PASS is blank, logging once which variable is missing plus the Gmail App Password steps. The user still has to fill SMTP_PASS for mail to actually send.

bugs.error_message: 'StartSonar.bat' is not recognized as an internal or external command, operable program or batch file
bugs.root_cause: Invoking the .bat by bare name after cd (via bash cmd //c, PowerShell Set-Location + cmd /c, or cmd /c "cd /d ... && StartSonar.bat") never resolves it, even though PATHEXT contains .BAT and the file exists. The shell wrapper does not resolve bare batch names against the new working directory.
bugs.fix: Invoke with an explicit full path through cmd call: cmd /c "call D:\SonarQube\sonarqube-26.4.0.121862\bin\windows-x86-64\StartSonar.bat" — run it as a background task since boot takes ~90s.

bugs.error_message: {"result":"Password must be at least 12 characters long"} — HTTP 400 from api/users/change_password
bugs.root_cause: After repointing SonarQube at the external Postgres the schema was fresh, so admin reverted to admin/admin and had to be reset. SonarQube 26.x enforces a 12-character minimum on api/users/change_password; the first attempt used <11-char-password> (11 chars) and was rejected with HTTP 400.
bugs.fix: Used a 12+ character password (<sonarqube-admin-password>). Also had to mint a brand new SONAR_TOKEN afterwards — the pre-switch token belonged to the old H2 schema and no longer existed.

bugs.error_message: Too many failed attempts. Try again in 15 minutes. (HTTP 429) then Cannot reach the agent. Is the server running?
bugs.root_cause: User typed <a-wrong-password> instead of the actual password <dashboard-admin-password>, tripping the login rate limiter at server.js:711 — loginAttempts is an in-memory Map keyed by IP, 8 failures per 15-minute window. The follow-up unreachable error was self-inflicted: the fix restarts the process, and the user refreshed during the ~2s boot gap.
bugs.fix: Killed the node process on :3002 (taskkill /F) and ran npm start again — the lockout lives only in process memory, so a restart clears it instantly; no 15-minute wait is needed. Verified with a curl login returning HTTP 200. There is no persisted lockout and no unlock endpoint.

bugs.error_message: Report header said "252 total" while the severity bar and issue table only covered 50 findings
bugs.root_cause: fetchSonarReport() made a single call to /api/issues/search with ps=50. It read  from the response (the real count) but only ever kept the first page of issues, so every derived summary silently disagreed with the headline number.
bugs.fix: Paginate at ps=500 (Sonar API max) up to a 2000-issue cap, accumulating across pages. Verified: a scan reporting 285 issues now renders all 285 (severity bar sums 6+142+137) and the XML contains 285 <issue> elements.

bugs.error_message: ReferenceError: missing is not defined — thrown from sendEmail(), surfaced in the review log as "missing is not defined" immediately after "Sending report by email..."
bugs.root_cause: When sendEmail() was changed to return a status object instead of returning silently, the new return statement referenced `missing` — a const declared inside the nested `if (!smtpWarned)` block. const is block-scoped, so it was never visible at the return statement. It threw on every call, not just the first: the declaration site and the use site were in different scopes regardless of the warn-once flag. Compounding it, the email call had no try/catch of its own, so the throw propagated to the review handler's outer catch and reported the entire review as failed — even though the AI review had completed and report #6 was already stored in Postgres.
bugs.fix: Hoisted the `missing` const out of the `if (!smtpWarned)` block so the warn-once console output and the returned reason string no longer share a scope. Also wrapped the whole email step in its own try/catch: notification is the last and least important stage of the flow, so a mail failure now logs a warning instead of discarding a completed review and a stored report.

bugs.error_message: User: hovering near the top of the HTML report turned the whole area white
bugs.root_cause: The enhancement stylesheet carried an unscoped rule: tbody tr:hover { background:#fff7fb !important }. The report is built almost entirely from nested LAYOUT tables (masthead, stat tiles, section headings), and every one of those has an implicit tbody. Hovering anywhere over them repainted the pink gradient masthead and the metric tiles to the near-white hover tint. The !important made it override the inline gradient.
bugs.fix: Added class=dt to data tables only and scoped the rule to .dt tbody tr:hover, so the hover tint applies to report rows and never to layout scaffolding. Verified: masthead stays pink under the cursor, and a data row still tints to rgb(255,247,251).
